messages:
alex: FYI repro: qwen-mqa long-context job showing steady mem growth -> KV page cascade + kernel fallback. p95 latency spikes after ~18k tokens. attaching minimal trace below.

mira: can you paste the trace snippet and the kernel selection log?

alex: sure, pasted snippet: ```
[profile] seq=19000 tokens, kv_pages=243, kv_frag=0.62, slab_free=12MB
[kernel] selected=optimized_conv_v3, fallback=generic_attn when rope_scale!=1.0
[alloc] page_alloc_slow=0.34s, page_move=12ms
```

jon: hm sounds like fragmentation + small-page churn. MQA's per-head slot size can make page boundaries misalign with our slab sizes. saw something vaguely similar on mistral but different thresholds.

sasha: quick experiment idea: set KV_PAGE_SIZE=64k and force compact-sweep interval to 30s, see if page cascade stops. also try forcing kernel=optimized_conv_v2 to skip autotune.

alex: ran that locally — KV_PAGE_SIZE=64k reduced page-count by ~18%, p95 improved ~12%, but when rope_scale != 1.0 we still see kernel switch and a ~2x drop in throughput.

perf-bot: perf-regression alert: branch=main commit=ab12c3 delta_p95=+14% for qwen-mqa/longseq (compare baseline 12h).

oliver: how deterministic is the kernel fallback? is it reactive to memory pressure or to observed attention pattern (e.g., rope rescale causing different key/value layout)?

alex: looks reactive to two signals: (1) estimated GPU shared memory pressure (our allocator), (2) a kernel capability check that flags unsupported sequence/rope combos. when either tripped we pick generic_attn.

mira: that kernel capability check was conservative for MQA historically. maybe we can relax for qwen variants where we verified numeric stability. but need regression tests.

jon: I profiled KV reuse: reuse_ratio drops below 0.4 after a long prefix with GQA->MQA transitions (clients switching models mid-session). leads to more cold page allocs and fragmentation.

sasha: interesting — do we also observe increased page splits? i.e., allocator splitting a larger free run leading to tiny leftovers that never coalesce?

alex: yes. allocator logs show repeated split at same slab offset. looks like a pattern: requests with rope_scale ~1.25 cause alignment shift, new KVs land on different slot offsets than warm pages. over time small residual free fragments accumulate.

oliver: sounds like we need three actions: (A) add a model-aware slab alignment tweak (align slab base to model slot gcd), (B) relax kernel capability gating for qwen-mqa under validated bit-exact tests, (C) add a short-term compaction pass triggered when fragment_util > 0.45.

mira: +1. also add microbench harness for rope scaling edgecases (1.0 -> 1.25 -> 0.8) and automated acceptance.

alex: I'll prototype (A) this afternoon and run AB test with KV_PAGE_SIZE=64k. will post a small perf diff. assigning self.

jon: I'll work with mira on (B) — we'll run numeric stability suite on qwen-mqa variants and produce whitelist.

sasha: I'll put a draft compaction patch (C) behind a feature flag, we can enable on a few Dedicated shards to see behavioral change before global roll.

perf-bot: note: please link perf diffs back to the alert ticket (#perf-1746) so SRE can monitor.

alex: thanks — will update thread with diffs. short-term mitigation: recommend setting kernel_autotune=false for heavy longseq qwen-mqa routes until whitelist is out. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mira: nice plan. low-risk rollout path is important.

jon: leaving a note: this is an orthogonal source of memory growth to the existing KV-sweep bug we fixed last quarter — different root cause (alignment + kernel gating).

sasha: cool. I'll spin up canary config later today and report back. :rocket:
